clue.text: Fear of firework finally going off in parliament

indicators.note: the trimmed firework sits inside the word for parliament

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Diet of Japan

indicators.note: the firework word loses its final letter, which has gone off

parts.note: a squib is a small firework

explanation.surface: Anxiety in a legislature after a firework is set off inside it, perhaps recalling the Gunpowder Plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' looks like an explosion but means the firework word loses its end; a diet is a formal assembly, as in Japan's.
explanation.definitionFit: Disquiet is a state of unease or worry, a near synonym for fear.

clue.text: Absurd way dispute ends?

definitions.meaning: silly or pointless, an adjective sense
the way the word 'dispute' ends is '...', its final letter

explanation.surface: A wry remark that quarrels tend to finish in silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the answer as three words: IN AN E, describing how the word 'dispute' finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and lacking sense, which is close to absurd.

clue.text: One suit, perhaps, for officers on board

definitions.meaning: a single suit of cards is a quarter of a pack of playing cards
the officers of a ship collectively, named after the part of the deck they use

explanation.surface: Choosing a uniform for naval officers aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A deck of cards has four suits, so one suit is a quarter of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear upper deck is reserved for a ship's officers, and by extension the term names those officers themselves.

clue.text: Fashionable bit I do on old times for TV

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so these words are reworked

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Someone does a trendy little turn on a programme about the past for television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' looks like an adjective meaning trendy but is a verb form signalling the letters are shaped anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiot box is a disparaging slang name for a television set.

clue.text: How to clue crossword at last in most remote spot?

definitions.text: How to clue crossword at last
definitions.meaning: the last letter of crossword is D, which could be clued as the end letter of the word beyond

explanation.surface: A setter wonders how to clue a puzzle while stuck somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter of 'crossword' is D, which is also the back letter of 'beyond', so the phrase is a way to clue that D.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for any extremely remote, isolated place.

clue.text: Put pressure on after son becomes loutish

indicators.note: the pressure word comes after the son's letter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
to lobby is to press politicians for a cause

explanation.surface: A boy turns boorish after being pushed too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Slobby describes untidy, lazy and coarse behaviour, much like a lout's.

clue.text: Start series poorly

parts.note: a set is a series or collection of things
off means unwell or below par, as in feeling off

explanation.surface: A run of matches begins badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to start a journey or begin something.

clue.text: Chap rowing? No argument's stopped by him

indicators.note: the man rowing holds part of the phrase, so his name is lodged across the two words

explanation.surface: A rower is so imposing that nobody dares argue with him.
explanation.walkthrough: An oar can mean an oarsman, hence 'Chap rowing?'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is also used for a rower, the person who pulls the blade.

clue.text: Total ban originally covering one or many troops

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the numeral
done in an original, new way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A complete prohibition first applied to one soldier or a whole force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' reads like 'at first' but asks for the letters to be done in an original way; 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is a large army unit, so it holds many soldiers.

clue.text: Floor covering is so long — 880 yards

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, like so long
880 yards is half a mile, so half of the word mile

explanation.surface: A rug that measures half a mile in length.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatami is a Japanese straw mat used to cover floors.

clue.text: Sum being in possession of some troops?

indicators.note: the being holds the troops inside it

parts.note: an entity is a being, something that exists
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Asking about the total of a creature that owns an army.
explanation.definitionFit: The entirety is the whole amount, the total, which is what a sum is.

clue.text: Big hit for a band

definitions.meaning: a strip worn round the waist, or any encircling strap

explanation.surface: A popular song that suits a music group.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a heavy blow and a strap round the waist.

clue.text: Truck to fix could make driver late

parts.note: to have truck with is to have dealings, as is traffic
a jam is a tight spot or predicament, a fix

explanation.surface: A lorry needing repair could hold up a motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: Truck is not a lorry here but dealings, as in 'have no truck with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary queues of vehicles hold up motorists and so make them arrive late.

clue.text: One theme of Oliver Twist or a minor work

definitions.meaning: Dickens's novel shows orphans made to toil in workhouses
employment done by someone under age

explanation.surface: Discussing a Dickens novel's themes or one of an author's lesser pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor work' looks like a lesser piece of writing but is labour done by a minor.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means employing children, a theme of the novel and literally work by a minor.

clue.text: Plant growing wild daily by stretch of canal

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char
a lock is a section of canal between gates

explanation.surface: A wild plant growing beside a cleaning lady near a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing wild' looks like an anagram signal for 'daily' but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlock is wild mustard, a common weed of fields.

clue.text: Legendary time, one eg Horace recollected

indicators.note: gathered together again, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet such as Horace remembers a legendary era.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroic age is the mythical era of heroes in Greek legend.

clue.text: Goddess appearing in short book twice

indicators.note: the abbreviation is written out two times

parts.note: Is is the abbreviation for the Book of Isaiah

explanation.surface: A goddess turns up twice in a brief volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a principal goddess of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Works not started after composer makes judgments

indicators.note: the trimmed works come after the composer

parts.note: Verdi is the Italian opera composer

indicators.note: the word for works loses its opening letter

parts.note: acts are deeds or works

explanation.surface: Critics pass judgment on a composer's unfinished compositions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not started' takes the A from ACTS, leaving CTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdicts are the decisions or judgments reached, especially by juries.

clue.text: Strongly desire doctor once son's no longer around

indicators.note: the son's letters, which were around the outside, are removed

parts.note: a surgeon is a kind of doctor
the word son itself, taken out of the doctor

explanation.surface: A medic yearns for something now their son has gone away.
explanation.walkthrough: S and ON sit around URGE in SURGEON; removing them leaves the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge is to press or desire strongly, as in a verb of strong wanting.

clue.text: Dealing with a British writer

definitions.meaning: handling questions or a ball, as in cricket

explanation.surface: Negotiating with a novelist from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Fielding means handling or dealing with, and Henry Fielding was an English novelist.

clue.text: TV presenter in dock

definitions.meaning: the main presenter of a news programme
to moor a ship, holding it fast

explanation.surface: A broadcaster appears in the dock in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a news presenter, and as a verb means to moor a vessel.

clue.text: Be seen with a drink he or ordered? Port, say

indicators.note: put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is seen with a drink he asked for, perhaps a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink he ordered but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Birkenhead is a port town on the Wirral, across the Mersey from Liverpool.

clue.text: United win at Chelsea constantly

definitions.meaning: Manchester United beating Chelsea on Chelsea's ground is a win on the road
continuously, as in working on and on

explanation.surface: A football team keeps winning at a rival's London stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club; a win on the opponent's ground is called an away win.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a match on an opponent's ground, and also means continually, as in chatting on and on.

clue.text: Beer froth seen regularly on guard

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: every other letter of froth is taken

explanation.surface: Foam on a pint keeps appearing on cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert means watchful and ready, as a sentry on guard is.

clue.text: Dance with brute, avoiding a fuss

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: the brute word goes without the A

parts.note: a yahoo is a coarse, brutish person, from Gulliver's Travels
the letter A, which is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone escapes a rough partner at a dance and the result is a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops A from YAHOO, leaving YHOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy publicity or a great commotion.

clue.text: On stage

definitions.meaning: the on side in cricket is also called the ... side
a section of a journey or race, as in a stage of a tour

explanation.definitionFit: Leg is the cricket name for the on side, and a leg is a stage of a journey.

clue.text: Prison game where one must get caught first

indicators.note: the caught letter must move to the front of the game

parts.note: hockey is a field or ice game
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A game where a player has to be caught out before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Chokey is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Chokey is an old slang word for a jail or a prison cell.

clue.text: Physicist — one involved in rejection of Réaumur scale, say, repeatedly

indicators.note: the numeral is put inside the turned letters
rejecting turns these letters back to front

parts.note: R is the symbol for the Réaumur temperature scale

indicators.note: the example abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A scientist is caught up in discarding an old temperature scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns R EG EG into GEGER, and 'involved in' puts I inside to make the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Geiger was the German physicist who devised the radiation counter.

clue.text: Individual is tactful on the radio

indicators.note: broadcast speech is heard, not seen, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: discreet means careful and tactful

explanation.surface: A person who behaves tactfully when broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, as individual items are.
